narr: A stationary front over southern Missouri along with ample mid-level forcing, moisture, and efficient rain processes resulted in flooding across portions of east-central and southeast Missouri. Numerous roads across the St. Louis metropolitan area were impassable due to the heavy rainfall.
ev: Multiple instances of flash flooding were reported in St. Louis County due to heavy rain. Reports of flash flooding varied across the county. One report stated there was 2 to 3 feet of standing water on a road adjacent to Wildhorse Creek near Chesterfield. Another was of a stranded vehicle at the intersection of I-70 and I-270. Cold Water Creek also rose out of its banks in Hazelwood and entered the parking garage of the Hazelwood Civic Center on Dunn Road. The same creek came about 1 foot from reaching businesses on Bypasse Drive in Hazelwood. There was also a public report of roads closed due to flooding in Oakville. Rainfall amounts across the county vary from 2.5 to 6.3 inches ending on April 6th.

Heavy rain caused Joachim Creek to rise out of its banks near Crystal City and Valles Mill and caused Saline Creek to rise out of its banks in Jefferson County west of Fults, IL. Up to 7 inches of rain fell in portions of Jefferson County between April 4th and the evening of April 5th.

Heavy rain caused a few road closures in Jefferson County. One road closure was near Regina on Missouri BB and Regina Road. Here, downed power poles were reported. The other was near Imperial around US Highway 61/67 and Scott Lane/Mill Creek Drive/Montebello Road.

Multiple water rescues were reported in St. Francois County, one in Blackwell and another in an unnamed location in northern St. Francois County. Near Libertyville, an estimated 3 feet of water was running swiftly across Highway DD into a small lake across the street. The lake was reportedly spilling onto the road.

An emergency manager reported multiple vehicles trapped in high water on I-70 eastbound under the East Carrie Street overpass. This is a low area. A vehicle was also trapped in flood waters in St. Louis at Lindell Boulevard and Vandeventer Avenue. These areas received between 2 and 4 inches of rain.

Heavy rain resulted in lots of running water over Highway 94 near Terri Road. This made the road completely impassable. Near St. Paul, there were reports of heavy flooding north of Dalbow Road, though the extent of the flooding is unknown. Otherwise, there was a report of Dardenne Creek overflowing in St. Peters. This area received anywhere from 3 to 6.5 inches of rain over the duration of the event.

The Department of Highways and the public reported multiple inaccessible roads in Franklin County due to flooding. These include parts of Highway A and Highway YY due to side ditches overflowing and Highway CC due to Big Creek flooding over the road and onto the other side. Notably, this is a low point on the highway. On April 5th, the Missouri Department of Transportation reported that Route W just past Sand Ford Road at the entrance to Meramec Caverns was closing due to flooding of the Meramec River. Franklin County received up to 6.2 inches of rain during this event.

Several road closures were reported mainly in the Ellington area has rainwater flooded roadways and areal creeks overflowed. Examples of road closures include: MO 106 1 mile west of Route F, Route B between CR 785 and CR 784, and CR 838 at its intersection with CR 837. Logan Creek overflowed, making its bridge on Route B impassable and causing extensive damage to the bridge.

The Missouri Department of Transportation has reported multiple road closures in Iron County due to flooding that began on April 3rd. Some of these closures continued into May. Road closures include: Route F from CR 160 to CR 135, Route 40 at Route BB, and Route F from Missouri 49 to CR 165. Over the duration of the event, portions of Iron County received up to 7.5 inches of rain.

Fourche a Du Clos flooded over Highway Y at Jackson School Road deeming it impassable through the first low bottom bridge headed eastbound. A water rescue was reported at this location. On April 5th, water was reported over the roadway near Missouri 32. During the event, portions of Ste. Genevieve County received 3.75 to 6.25 inches of rainfall.
The Dent Branch of the Big River was reportedly swiftly running over Highway C where a bridge crosses the road. Rainfall totals through the event were on the order of 2.5 to 4.3 inches.

The 911 Call Center reported numerous events in Fredericktown including water over the roadway at Morley St and Villar St, City Lake Road, Buford Boulevard, Highway Z and North Chamber Drive, the 200 block of East College, and North Main Street. Southeast of town, Route F was closed where it meets Route V due to flooding. During the event, up to 7.75 inches of rain fell in Madison County.
